rows.label: Increase in syphilis testing rate by switching to dual RDT

source.title: Source spreadsheet
source.cell: Version A - costs shifted to ch!B14

rows.explainer: 95 (current HIV screening rate) - 56.5 (current syphilis screening rate) = 38.5 pp https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pwZ-H2XJXYT9nquOr5REh7tzTiN7nLAtHxeGUT2A3fY/edit#gid=106031938 I assume rapid tests have a higehr follow up rate too than lab tests so this would be quite conservative if that is what it is capturing This just captures the extra percentage of the population that would get screened if we switched to the dual RDTs, i.e. screening rate would go from the current 56.5% to 95% (= screening rate for HIV), which is a 38.5pp difference

source.title: Source spreadsheet
source.cell: Version A - costs shifted to ch!B12

rows.explainer:
Only one dose of BPG is needed. BPG is typically available at US$0.50 per dose in low- and middle-income countries
May be even lower; According to this paper, the price may be as low as $0.11 per dose: https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1002473 https://medaccess.org/news/new-partnership-increase-access-dual-rapid-testing-syphilis-hiv/

summary: Ambitious Impact's 2023 estimate for a new charity that helps governments roll out dual HIV/syphilis rapid tests and penicillin treatment in antenatal clinics, modelled for Ghana. The idea Healthy Futures was founded to run. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet, traced cell by cell from its bottom line: the cost per DALY averted counting both charity and government costs (the current sheet gives $92; the report quoted $81).
